# The Floor {#sec-floor}

The trichotomy of @sec-theorem states what fails *above* a floor. The
floor itself is not a fourth axis or a residual category for whatever
does not fit the other three; it is exactly two residuals, one per
component of the realized commitment pair $(C, V)$ — the physical
half of the model that no amount of record structure can reach.

**The binding residual** (on $C$'s side). Every commitment ultimately
rests on a physical hardness assumption — a hash function's collision
resistance, a signature scheme's forgery resistance — that is not itself
a claim about a record and so is not a candidate for the trichotomy to
classify. Its admission test is marginal necessity: a hardness
assumption belongs to the floor exactly when removing it removes the
commitment's binding property entirely, with no substitute available
inside the model. The mechanization keeps this boundary visible — the
commitment's binding and verification conditions are hypotheses of the
*Commitment* structure, supplied by the instantiator, never derived.

**The fidelity residual** (on $V$'s side). A verifier is, physically, a
running program, and no record-side argument can establish that the
program executing right now is the one that was specified. Thompson's
construction is exactly this residual, and it was constructive from the
start rather than rhetorical [@thompson-1984]: a compiler — or a
verifier — can be made to insert behavior that no inspection of its
source recovers. Its
admission test is a diagonalization argument: for any purely
record-side verification of "this execution is faithful," a
faithfulness-violating execution can be constructed that the
verification cannot distinguish from a faithful one.

The count is not asserted by enumeration; it follows from what a scheme
*is*. A scheme realizes exactly two operative components, and each is
where the model's abstractions bottom out in something physical. A third
residual would require a third realized component in a scheme's
signature, and none exists — the same discipline the trichotomy itself
uses, where the count is a consequence of the structure being counted.

Both residuals are unmechanized. They concern physical realization
rather than the record-and-context model of @sec-model. What is
mechanized is everything *above* the floor — the claim that,
once a binding commitment and a faithful verifier are granted, exactly
three further reasons can defeat verification, and no others.
